thesis.title: Approach to AI implementation in regulated enterprise environments

stages.title: Find the real bottleneck
stages.question: Where does time, effort, and coordination overhead actually accumulate?
stages.method: Start with the people who do the work. Interview process owners, observe workflows directly, and build a simple model of what the current process actually costs before touching any technology.
stages.output: A ranked shortlist of workflow candidates with rough economics attached
stages.example: Non-financial-risk teams (RCSA, TPRM, control testing) typically spend most of their time gathering the same information from different systems. The bottleneck is usually coordination and synthesis, not the analysis itself.

stages.title: Map who owns the problem and who controls the budget
stages.question: Who experiences the pain, who has the authority to act, and who must approve?
stages.method: Stakeholder mapping from executive sponsor down through the process owner to the technology team. The key question is whether the person with the problem controls the budget or needs to build a case upward.
stages.output: A clear picture of who needs to say yes and what each of them needs to see
stages.example: In regulated financial services, the CRO often sponsors, operations owns delivery, and the CIO gates the integration. Alignment across all three is usually a precondition for successful delivery.

stages.title: Measure the current state before building anything
stages.question: What does this process actually cost in analyst time, cycle time, and downstream rework?
stages.method: Document analyst hours, cycle times, error rates, and rework. A concrete baseline is what makes the business case credible and sets the performance target the implementation will be measured against.
stages.output: A documented baseline and a business case framing that connects current cost to investment threshold
stages.example: A DORA evidence-generation cycle that ties up multiple analysts for several weeks has a calculable cost. That number drives the investment conversation before a single line of code is written.

stages.title: Build the hard part first
stages.question: Can a working demonstrator show that the most difficult piece actually functions?
stages.method: Prototype the core workflow using realistic synthetic data. The most valuable demonstrators focus on the technically difficult parts (agent orchestration, integration, edge-case handling) and include an honest evaluation of what works and what does not.
stages.output: A working demonstrator with an evaluation of capabilities and limitations
stages.example: The NFR platform and DORA control-line builds are structured around this: real agent orchestration, real integration patterns, real human-approval gates, evaluated against defined criteria.

stages.title: Wire into real systems with human oversight built in
stages.question: Where does the data originate and where do humans stay in control of consequential decisions?
stages.method: Map data flows from source systems through agent processing to write-back destinations. Every consequential output needs a human approval gate. The system should support human judgment, not bypass it.
stages.output: Integration architecture and documented control framework
stages.example: In practice this means ServiceNow for records, Teams or Power Automate for approvals, and policy-engine verification before anything is written back to the systems of record.

stages.title: Measure the result and package the pattern
stages.question: Did it work, and can the same approach be applied to the next workflow?
stages.method: Define success metrics before go-live. Measure cycle-time reduction, analyst hours saved, output acceptance rate, and human override rate. Then document the architecture and commercial template so the next use case starts from a better base.
stages.output: A measured result, a reference architecture, and a reusable template
stages.example: One paid engagement should produce a documented baseline, a working integration, a measured outcome, and an architecture that makes the next workflow faster to implement, in the same organisation or a different one.

projects.title: Enterprise NFR Agent Platform
projects.problem: Non-financial-risk work is fragmented across service-management records, controls, policies, regulatory information, documents, and manual analyst workflows.
projects.summary: Enterprise platform built around multiple AI agent workflows, each handling a different NFR domain, with a shared knowledge graph, document intelligence, regulatory analysis, human approval gates, and enterprise integration patterns. Built as a technical demonstrator of what a production-grade enterprise AI stack looks like in practice.
projects.commercial: Individual AI use cases tend to stay isolated from each other. This platform shows what it looks like when they share a knowledge graph, common agent infrastructure, and consistent approval patterns: the architecture of a platform rather than a collection of disconnected pilots.
projects.diagram: Systems of record → documents & data → knowledge graph → agent orchestration → human approval → enterprise write-back
projects.limitations: Synthetic demonstration · no client data · not a production deployment
projects.caseStudy: Each agent handles a specific NFR domain: RCSA, TPRM, regulatory change. A shared knowledge graph maintains the relationships between controls, policies, and regulatory obligations across domains. Document intelligence processes unstructured content from multiple source types. Every consequential output routes through a human approval gate before anything is written back to systems of record. Integration patterns are modelled on real enterprise environments, ServiceNow for records, Teams for approvals, built entirely on synthetic data without any client credentials.

projects.title: DORA Article 12 AI Control Line
projects.problem: Regulatory change (DORA Article 12) is typically translated manually through policy, controls, infrastructure, verification, documentation, and audit evidence, a process that spans weeks and multiple teams.
projects.summary: A fully functional AI workflow demonstrator built around a real regulatory requirement (DORA Article 12). Uses synthetic and anonymized data throughout. Takes a regulatory input through AI-generated control updates, infrastructure proposals, policy-engine verification, compliance documentation, human approval gates, and a complete traceable evidence chain.
projects.commercial: Demonstrates the full architecture of an enterprise AI workflow: model integration (OpenAI o3 for regulatory reasoning, GPT-4o for infrastructure, GPT-4o-mini for documentation), an 11-state machine for end-to-end traceability, and human approval gates at every consequential step. Built using only synthetic and anonymized data.
projects.diagram: Regulation → AI guideline proposal → AI control design → AI infrastructure change → policy verification → compliance work product → AI documentation → evidence package
projects.limitations: Demonstrator using synthetic and anonymized data · no client systems, credentials, or confidential information · integration patterns are illustrative
projects.caseStudy: Built around a DORA Article 12 regulatory requirement using synthetic and anonymized data only. The workflow routes through OpenAI o3 for regulatory reasoning and control design, GPT-4o for infrastructure code generation, and GPT-4o-mini for documentation. An 11-state machine provides full traceability from regulatory input to artefact. Human approval gates are embedded at each consequential decision point. The AI provider layer is abstracted so the architecture is not locked to any single model. Tests cover the full workflow including edge cases and human-override paths. The architecture reflects patterns from enterprise delivery experience.

projects.title: Enterprise AI Economics Simulator
projects.problem: Enterprise buyers struggle to connect model usage, hosting, shared-platform costs, governance, and expected gains to an all-in AI business case.
projects.summary: Interactive tool for modelling the full economics of an enterprise AI platform: model selection and routing, token costs, cloud vs. sovereign vs. on-premise hosting, shared infrastructure costs, governance overhead, and net value projections. Built for executive decision-making and proposal development.
projects.commercial: Useful for buyers and architects who need to model the full economics of an AI platform investment: not only capability but also what shared infrastructure and governance overhead do to unit economics.
projects.diagram: Model selection → usage assumptions → hosting scenario → shared platform costs → governance overhead → net economics
projects.limitations: All prices, benchmarks, gains, and allocation values are illustrative planning assumptions.
projects.caseStudy: Built for enterprise buyers and architects who need to make defensible investment decisions about AI platforms. Covers model selection and routing strategy, token-cost modelling across providers, hosting scenario comparison (cloud, sovereign, on-premise), shared-platform cost amortization, governance overhead allocation, and projected value gains. Outputs are scenario-comparable and designed to support structured proposal development.

projects.title: AI Model Risk Dashboard
projects.problem: Enterprises adopting AI lack a structured way to inventory, monitor, and govern AI models across regulatory frameworks (NIST AI RMF, DORA, SR 11-7, GDPR) leaving risk invisible until it surfaces in an audit.
projects.summary: Production-ready dashboard for AI model risk management structured around the NIST AI RMF phases (Govern / Map / Measure / Manage). Covers model inventory, shadow AI detection, regulatory heat-mapping across multiple frameworks, vendor risk assessment, and an immutable audit trail.
projects.commercial: AI governance is becoming a board-level topic, but most organisations lack the tooling to operationalise it. This dashboard translates regulatory frameworks (NIST, DORA, SR 11-7) into a manageable inventory with live risk signals, useful for CROs and AI governance functions establishing structured oversight.
projects.diagram: Model inventory → regulatory heat-map → shadow AI detection → vendor risk → audit trail
projects.limitations: Demonstrator using synthetic data · no client models, credentials, or production data
projects.caseStudy: Structured around the NIST AI RMF lifecycle phases. Regulatory mapping covers DORA, SR 11-7, GDPR, and the EU AI Act. Shadow AI detection flags ungoverned model usage across the organisation. Vendor risk module covers third-party model dependencies. Audit trail is append-only and timestamped, supporting audit-readiness requirements.

projects.title: Autonomous Operations Control Center
projects.problem: Autonomous AI-driven operations are difficult to demonstrate credibly: the governance layer, real-time state transitions, and human approval gates are invisible in static slides or disconnected prototypes.
projects.summary: Full-stack demonstrator of autonomous AI-driven IT operations. A 3-minute guided scenario runs a real backend state machine with SSE-driven live UI updates and a human-in-the-loop governance gate at consequential decision points.
projects.commercial: Demonstrates what a credible autonomous-operations build looks like in practice: a real state machine driving live UI updates, with a human approval gate embedded at decisions that matter. Structured to be walkthroughable in three minutes for an executive audience.
projects.diagram: Event ingestion → autonomous triage → state machine → human approval gate → action execution → audit log
projects.limitations: Demonstrator using synthetic events · no production system credentials or client data
projects.caseStudy: Backend state machine tracks every transition with a full audit log. SSE pushes real-time state to the UI without polling. Human approval gate intercepts consequential decisions before execution, maintaining a clear record of what was approved, by whom, and when. The three-minute guided scenario is designed to make the governance layer visible and credible to a non-technical buyer.

projects.title: AIRLOCK: AWS Regulated AI Workload Foundry
projects.problem: Regulated enterprises need AI agent workflows that are fully auditable, have human approval at every consequential decision, and can be deployed on compliant cloud infrastructure, but no credible reference architecture exists for this combination.
projects.summary: Reference implementation for building auditable, human-approved AI agent workflows on AWS for regulated industries. Demo workload is a Primary Markets bond structuring assistant using synthetic data. Includes a fully functional local-mode implementation and Terraform infrastructure modules for AWS deployment.
projects.commercial: Bridges the gap between an AI proof-of-concept and a production-grade regulated deployment. Shows the full stack: auditable agent orchestration, human approval gates, and the Terraform modules for a compliant AWS deployment, structured as a reusable foundry pattern rather than a one-off build.
projects.diagram: Workflow trigger → agent orchestration → human approval gate → audit record → AWS deployment layer
projects.limitations: Demo workload uses synthetic data only · AWS/Terraform mode is reference architecture, not a deployed production environment
projects.caseStudy: Local mode is fully functional and runnable without cloud infrastructure. AWS/Terraform modules define the compliant deployment pattern with the necessary controls for a regulated environment. Every agent action is logged with full provenance. Human approval gates are embedded at consequential steps. Structured as a reusable foundry pattern: a second workload reuses the same orchestration, approval, and audit infrastructure.

projects.title: Interactive Personal Story
projects.problem: Translating a personal narrative into an engaging, accessible single-page experience.
projects.summary: An interactive single-page experience combining personal storytelling, data visualization, accessibility, and lightweight product design.
projects.commercial: Demonstrates product thinking, design sensibility, and the ability to work across the full stack independently.
projects.diagram: Content design → visual layout → interaction design → accessibility → deployment
projects.caseStudy: A personal side project exploring the intersection of storytelling and product design. Built entirely in vanilla web technologies with attention to accessibility, motion, and visual hierarchy. Demonstrates independent product thinking outside of an enterprise context.

commercialization.title: Approach to a first commercial engagement
commercialization.label: Commercial engagement hypothesis
commercialization.icp: Bank, insurer, or regulated financial institution · significant operational-risk, compliance, or regulatory function · data distributed across documents, GRC systems, service-management platforms, and spreadsheets · active transformation around DORA, AI governance, RCSA, TPRM, or regulatory change · CRO, COO, or Head of NFR with sponsorship authority
commercialization.wedge: Start with one specific, measurable workflow (DORA evidence generation, RCSA refresh, control-gap analysis, or third-party-risk change triage) where the current cost is documentable and the improvement is demonstrable.
commercialization.offer: A six-to-eight-week paid engagement covering baseline measurement, data readiness, workflow design, a working integrated demonstrator, human approval gates, evaluation criteria, economic modelling, and a production roadmap.
path: Confirm the problem and measure the baseline
Establish data access and environment readiness
Design and build the core workflow
Package the pattern as a reusable asset
commercialization.metricsLabel: Proposed measurement dimensions, not historical performance claims

periods.label: Days 1–30
periods.heading: Listen, map, and orient
items: Understand the product boundaries and market positioning
Build a picture of existing customers and ecosystem relationships
Define an initial target customer profile and qualification criteria
Identify the most credible near-term commercial entry point
Agree with stakeholders on what good looks like by day 90

periods.label: Days 31–60
periods.heading: Engage and test
items: Run customer discovery conversations with target accounts
Develop and refine initial commercial proposals
Build or adapt a demonstrator that speaks to buyer priorities
Document blockers and open questions transparently

periods.label: Days 61–90
periods.heading: Deliver, measure, and document
items: Begin or complete first paid design engagement
Establish workflow baselines to measure against
Produce first reusable commercial and technical templates
Map adjacent workflows and expansion opportunities
